description: We are a team working on the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge, building a web app that makes satellite fire records easier to explore. We're looking for teammates with skills in Python/data processing, frontend development, data visualization or statistics, and someone to help with the demo video and presentation. Beginners are welcome. Message us to join!
summary:
MODIS (since 2000) and VIIRS (since 2012) have tracked active fires from space for decades, but their records cannot be compared directly: the sensors differ in pixel size (about 1 km vs 375 m) and sensitivity, so raw fire counts and fire radiative power (FRP) are not interchangeable. FIREWATCH is a web dashboard that puts them on a common scale. It calibrates weekly VIIRS FRP onto the MODIS scale using the years both sensors flew, then validates the result on years the model never saw (leave-one-year-out). Every country gets a High, Medium or Low confidence label.

Pick a country to explore a daily burning-activity calendar, switch between Raw and Harmonized views, browse a six-year calendar, compare any year with the typical day-of-year range, spot unusually active weeks (above the 90th percentile), and see estimated fire-season start, peak and end.

The packaged data cover 2020-2025 across 236 country labels (3,859 NASA FIRMS files). Median R² is 0.80 and median holdout error is about 41%; 67 countries are High confidence, 65 Medium and 104 Low. The tool supports early-warning research, response planning, science and land management. Results are preliminary (six-year baseline) statistical estimates, not a physical correction or an operational alert service.
details:
What it does and how it works

FIREWATCH is a country-level NASA FIRMS Standard Processing explorer. Select a country and year to inspect daily detections or FRP by sensor family. Empty dates do not prove there was no fire. The map shows one-degree cells and activity centroids, not perimeters or country boundaries. Export a yearly CSV or calendar PNG. The six-year view shows daily patterns, typical range, unusual weeks, and preliminary fire-season dates.

The harmonization method

Weekly vegetation-only FRP is fitted with a Theil–Sen log–log model predicting MODIS from VIIRS. Eligible weeks have ≥5 MW per family; country fits need ≥40 overlap weeks. Leave-one-year-out validation measures fit and holdout error. High requires R² ≥0.7 and MdAPE ≤0.35; Medium requires R² ≥0.4 and MdAPE ≤0.60. Other fits and the deterministic global fallback are Low. Paired estimates are combined in log space; otherwise the available family is used. The interval is ±1.96 residual log-space standard deviations. This is not a physical correction and cannot normalize observation opportunity.

Data used

The 2020–2025 package contains 3,859 country files and 265,659,156 rows across 236 country labels: MODIS Terra/Aqua and VIIRS Suomi-NPP and NOAA-20 Standard Processing (375 m VIIRS products). NOAA-21 and raw CSV archives are excluded.

Benefits and intended impact

Raw and calibrated views help researchers, responders, and land managers inspect activity, coverage, and confidence. FIREWATCH supports exploration; it is not an operational alert service.

Tools and languages

The interface uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Recharts, MapLibre GL JS, and Lucide React. Python and DuckDB build the aggregates; pandas and NumPy are imported by the calibration scripts. backend/requirements.txt omits pandas and NumPy, so fresh backend setup needs confirmation.

Creativity

A Raw sensors / Harmonized toggle, confidence labels, vegetation-only input, uncertainty bands, and preliminary labels make the method inspectable. Source provenance stays available for review and replacement.

Factors considered and limitations

Analysis uses FIRMS country labels, not custom areas. File coverage and platform-day flags do not measure observation opportunity; empty dates are not confirmed no-fire dates. The baseline is short, coverage varies, 104 fits are Low confidence, and NOAA-21 is absent. Validation does not establish sensor equivalence.

Next steps

After verifying files and storage, extend toward MODIS 2000 and VIIRS S-NPP 2012; add NOAA-21 with defensible country attribution, custom areas, and a verified boundary layer after expert review.
